arxiv-2012-00139.title: Model Adaptation for Inverse Problems in Imaging
arxiv-2012-00139.creator: Davis Gilton, Gregory Ongie, Rebecca Willett
arxiv-2012-00139.description: Abstract Deep neural networks have been applied successfully to a wide variety of inverse problems arising in computational imaging. These networks are typically trained using a forward model that describes the measurement process to be inverted, which is often incorporated directly into the network itself.

arxiv-2103-00503.title: Geometrical aspects of entropy production in stochastic thermodynamics based on Wasserstein distance
arxiv-2103-00503.creator: Muka Nakazato, Sosuke Ito
arxiv-2103-00503.description: Abstract We study a relationship between optimal transport theory and stochastic thermodynamics for the Fokker-Planck equation. We show that the lower bound on the entropy production is the action measured by the path length of the L 2 L^{2} -Wasserstein distance.

arxiv-2203-15627.creator: Arnold Filtser, Hung Le
arxiv-2203-15627.description: Abstract Cohen-Addad, Filtser, Klein and Le [FOCS’20] constructed a stochastic embedding of minor-free graphs of diameter D D into graphs of treewidth O ϵ ​ ( log ⁡ n ) O_{\epsilon}(\log n) with expected additive distortion + ϵ ​ D +\epsilon D . Cohen-Addad et al.

arxiv-2301-00420.title: X-Arapuca long term test
arxiv-2301-00420.creator: Y. Suvorov
arxiv-2301-00420.description: Abstract The photon detection system of the DUNE experiment is based on the X-ARAPUCA light trap. The basic elements of the X-ARAPUCA are the dichroic filters coated with wavelength shifter (para-Therphenyl), a waveshifting plate and an array of SiPMs which detects the trapped photons.

arxiv-2303-05634.title: Fusarium head blight detection, spikelet estimation, and severity assessment in wheat using 3D convolutional neural networks
arxiv-2303-05634.creator: Oumaima Hamila, Christopher J. Henry, Oscar I. Molina, Christopher P. Bidinosti, Maria Antonia Henriquez
arxiv-2303-05634.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Oumaima Hamila, Christopher J. Henry, Oscar I. Molina, Christopher P. Bidinosti, Maria Antonia Henriquez. Fusarium head blight (FHB) is one of the most significant diseases affecting wheat and other small grain cereals worldwide. The development of resistant varieties requires the laborious task of field and greenhouse phenotyping.

arxiv-2305-03829.title: Improving Image-Based Precision Medicine with Uncertainty-Aware Causal Models
arxiv-2305-03829.creator: Joshua Durso-Finley 1,4 , Jean-Pierre Falet 1,3,4 , Raghav Mehta 1,4 , Douglas L. Arnold 1,3 , Nick Pawlowski 2 , Tal Arbel 1,4
arxiv-2305-03829.description: Abstract Image-based precision medicine aims to personalize treatment decisions based on an individual’s unique imaging features so as to improve their clinical outcome. Machine learning frameworks that integrate uncertainty estimation as part of their treatment recommendations would be safer and more reliable. However, little work has been done in adapting uncertainty estimation techniques and validation metrics for precision medicine.

arxiv-2306-00131.title: Assessment of a Physics-based Retrieval of Exoplanet Atmospheric Temperatures from Infrared Emission Spectra 2023 Assessment of a Physics-based Retrieval of Exoplanet Atmospheric Temperatures from Infrared Emission Spectra – References
arxiv-2306-00131.creator: Franz Schreier, J. Lee Grenfell, Fabian Wunderlich, Thomas Trautmann
arxiv-2306-00131.description: Abstract Atmospheric temperatures are to be estimated from thermal emission spectra of Earth-like exoplanets orbiting M-stars as observed by current and future planned missions. To this end, a line-by-line radiative transfer code is used to generate synthetic thermal infrared (TIR) observations. The range of “observed” intensities provides a rough hint of the atmospheric temperature range without any a priori knowledge.

arxiv-2403-10271.title: SuperM2M: Supervised and Mixture-to-Mixture Co-Learning for Speech Enhancement and Noise-Robust ASR Journal: Neural Networks
arxiv-2403-10271.creator: Zhong-Qiu Wang
arxiv-2403-10271.description: Abstract The current dominant approach for neural speech enhancement is based on supervised learning by using simulated training data. The trained models, however, often exhibit limited generalizability to real-recorded data. To address this, this paper investigates training enhancement models directly on real target-domain data.

Compact systems like TOI-5398, with an outer close-orbit giant and an inner small-size planet, are rare among systems containing short-period giants.

arxiv-2407-08182.title: Beyond Text: Leveraging Multi-Task Learning and Cognitive Appraisal Theory for Post-Purchase Intention Analysis
arxiv-2407-08182.creator: Gerard Christopher Yeo, Shaz Furniturewala, Kokil Jaidka
arxiv-2407-08182.description: Abstract Supervised machine-learning models for predicting user behavior offer a challenging classification problem with lower average prediction performance scores than other text classification tasks. This study evaluates multi-task learning frameworks grounded in Cognitive Appraisal Theory to predict user behavior as a function of users’ self-expression and psychological attributes.

arxiv-2504-19490.title: Rapid and efficient wavefront correction for spatially entangled photons using symmetrized optimization
arxiv-2504-19490.creator: Kiran Bajar, Ronen Shekel, Vikas S. Bhat, Rounak Chatterjee, Yaron Bromberg, Sushil Mujumdar*
arxiv-2504-19490.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kiran Bajar, Ronen Shekel, Vikas S. Bhat, Rounak Chatterjee, Yaron Bromberg, Sushil Mujumdar*. Spatial entanglement is a key resource in quantum technologies, enabling applications in quantum communication, imaging, and computation. However, propagation through complex media distorts spatial correlations, posing a challenge for practical implementations. We introduce a symmetrized genetic algorithm (sGA) for adaptive wavefront correction of spatially entangled photons, leveraging the insight that only the even-parity component of wavefront distortions affects two-photon correlations.

arxiv-2602-15103.title: UV and Optical Signatures of Late-time Disk Instabilities in Tidal Disruption Events
arxiv-2602-15103.creator: Daichi Tsuna, V. Ashley Villar, Anthony L. Piro, Samantha C. Wu
arxiv-2602-15103.description: Abstract Tidal disruption events (TDEs) are unique probes of evolving accretion in supermassive black holes. Recent models of TDE disks show that they undergo brief thermal instabilities with temporal super-Eddington accretion at late times, which has been suggested as a possibility to explain the ubiquitous late radio emergence in TDEs.

britannica-1911-atlas.title: Atlas (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-atlas.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-atlas.description: Article 'Atlas' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 2), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The plural form Atlantes is the classical term in architecture for the male sculptured figures supporting a superstructure as in the baths at Pompeii, and in the temple at Agrigentum in Sicily. In 18th-century architecture half-figures of men with strong muscular development were used to support balconies (see Caryatides and Telamones).

pmc-11428911.title: Awareness of, willingness to use, and experiences with Pre-exposure prophylaxis among youth in Nigeria
pmc-11428911.creator: Titilola Gbaja-Biamila, Chisom Obiezu-Umeh, Ucheoma Nwaozuru, Nora E Rosenberg, Mesoma Igbokwe, David Oladele, Adesola Z Musa, Ifeoma Idigbe, Donaldson Conserve, Suzanne Day, Kadija Tahlil, Jason Ong, Kathryn Muessig, Susan Nkengasong, Hong Xian, Joseph D Tucker, Oliver Ezechi, Juliet Iwelunmor
pmc-11428911.description: BackgroundYouth (ages 14–24) in Nigeria have disproportionately high rates of new HIV infection. Pre-exposure prophylaxis could substantially reduce new infections among youth but has not been scaled up. This cross-sectional study aimed to assess Pre-exposure prophylaxis awareness, willingness to use, and prior use of Pre-exposure prophylaxis among youth in Nigeria.

pmc-11644739.title: Differentiation of Amaranthus Species and Estimation of Their Polyphenolic Compounds and Antioxidant Potential Using Near-Infrared Spectroscopy
pmc-11644739.creator: Svetoslava Terzieva, Neli Grozeva, Milena Tzanova, Petya Veleva, Mariya Gerdzhikova, Stefka Atanassova, Marcello Salvatore Lenucci
pmc-11644739.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Amaranthus species are rich in protein, fiber, minerals, and other nutrients and have various health benefits. The genus is taxonomically difficult due to the high phenotypic plasticity and the spontaneous interspecies introgression and hybridization between species. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the possibilities of near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for the taxonomic differentiation of some of the species common in Bulgaria and estimate their polyphenolic compounds. Tested samples were collected from six Bulgarian floristic regions: Amaranthus albus L., A.

pmc-11802568.title: MDTR: a knowledge-guided interpretable representation for quantifying liver toxicity at transcriptomic level
pmc-11802568.creator: Inyoung Sung, Sangseon Lee, Dongmin Bang, Jungseob Yi, Sunho Lee, Sun Kim
pmc-11802568.description: IntroductionDrug-induced liver injury (DILI) has been investigated at the patient level. Analysis of gene perturbation at the cellular level can help better characterize biological mechanisms of hepatotoxicity. Despite accumulating drug-induced transcriptome data such as LINCS, analyzing such transcriptome data upon drug treatment is a challenging task because the perturbation of expression is dose and time dependent.

pmc-12462738.title: Green Fluorescent Protein SELEX: Immobilization Chemistry and His‐Tag Epitope Bias
pmc-12462738.creator: Stefen Stangherlin, Tyler Malloch, Anthony J. Clarke, Juewen Liu
pmc-12462738.description: Despite numerous DNA aptamers for proteins having been reported, a model system allowing the use of cost‐effective proteins, unmodified DNA, and convenient homogeneous assays is still lacking, which has in turn limited not only fundamental studies of aptamers but also their translation to practical applications.

pmc-12535135.title: The needs of parents and their network to influence physical activity and motor development among children 0-to-4-years old: a mixed-methods study protocol
pmc-12535135.creator: Mary-ann R. Wagijo, Teatske M. Altenburg, Annick Ledebt, Floor Bartels, Robert K. van der Kaap, Katja Bel, Sanne Voorwinden, Corina van Doodewaard, Dave H. H. van Kann, Jessica S. Gubbels, Marleen H. M. de Moor, ASAS-consortium
pmc-12535135.description: BackgroundPromoting physical activity and motor development in early childhood is important for physical and mental health outcomes later in life. However, knowledge on how to influence physical activity and motor development in early life focusing on families and their context in daily life is currently lacking.

pmc-12651583.title: Purinergic Signaling in Swallowing Reflex Initiation: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications for Oropharyngeal Dysphagia—A Narrative Review
pmc-12651583.creator: Junrong Qi, Mohammad Zakir Hossain, Hiroshi Ando, Rita Rani Roy, Junichi Kitagawa
pmc-12651583.description: The swallowing reflex is a highly coordinated process that is essential for safe bolus transit and airway protection. Although its neurophysiological framework has been extensively studied, the molecular mechanisms underlying reflex initiation remain incompletely understood, limiting targeted therapies for oropharyngeal dysphagia.

pmc-12999245.title: Development and Validation of the Scale for Understanding Life-Oriented Expression and Dispositions
pmc-12999245.creator: Hyukjae Kwon, Sojung Hong, Sunhae Kim, Tae Hyun Sung, Kounseok Lee
pmc-12999245.description: Objective This study developed and validated the Scale for Understanding Life-Oriented Expression and Dispositions (SULEDIS), a self-report tool designed to assess adult dispositional orientations across multiple life domains. The SULEDIS addresses limitations in existing temperament and personality measures by capturing both motivational drives and relational context. Methods Researchers created the SULEDIS through theoretical review, expert consultation, and iterative item refinement.

pmc-13049826.title: Full-length haplotype reconstruction of CD36 by long-read sequencing: uncovers a novel structural variant
pmc-13049826.creator: Shuang Liang, Tong Liu, Huatao Che, Wenxia Xia, Weiyi Fu, Fan Wu, Liyan Sun, Yongshui Fu, Faming Zhu, Dawei Cui
pmc-13049826.description: PurposeCD36 deficiency predisposes to fetal/neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia (FNAIT) and platelet transfusion refractoriness (PTR), yet its genetic architecture remains incompletely understood. In particular, the contribution of large structural variants has been difficult to assess using conventional genotyping approaches. This study aimed to reconstruct full-length CD36 haplotypes using long-read sequencing and to systematically characterize its genetic architecture.

pmc-13234617.title: Effects of exposure to ethinyl estradiol during pregnancy and lactation on the postinvolution mammary gland
pmc-13234617.creator: Joshua P Mogus, Priyanka Maharaj-Chama, Laura N Vandenberg
pmc-13234617.description: ContextThe mammary gland undergoes extensive reorganization during pregnancy, lactation, and involution. During involution, mass apoptosis of epithelial cells and infiltration of immune cells return the gland to a state similar to the nulliparous female. However, the postinvolution gland has structural differences to the nulliparous gland, which may provide protection against breast cancer.

pmc-13303818.title: Genotype by light quality interaction on the growth and development of quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa) and the crop response to salinity
pmc-13303818.creator: Milton Gordillo-Romero, María de Lourdes Torres, Viviana Jaramillo Román, Daniel Dávila, Renato Morales-Acuña, Andrés F. Torres, Sofia D. Carvalho

pmc-13332205.title: Research on the stability of support structures in steeply dipping coal seam working face
pmc-13332205.creator: Yanhua Guo, Yanjie Zhang, Xian-gang Han, Teng-jiao Wang, Chi Zhu, Haoyu Song
pmc-13332205.description: Stability control of overlying strata and support equipment in steeply inclined coal seam faces poses a significant challenge in mining operations. The implementation of curved face layouts has been proven effective in enhancing support stability. This study establishes mechanical models for both sliding and toppling instability of supports in steeply inclined faces.

pmc-13414806.title: Achieving Exceptional Mechanical Properties of Epoxy Resins at Ultralow Loadings via a 3DGO@TiO2 Hybrid Filler
pmc-13414806.creator: Lizhe Liang, Lan Li, Qiyuan Li
pmc-13414806.description: Epoxy resin (EP) exhibits pronounced intrinsic brittleness arising from the highly crosslinked network formed after curing, thereby restricting its application in load-bearing structures. Although TiO2 nanoparticles possess the potential for impact-strength improvement, they are highly prone to aggregation, which compromises stress-transfer efficiency within the composite.
